screens.title: How many steps?
screens.text: This AVL tree holds 16 keys. What is the most comparisons a search can need?
screens.reveal: 5. The tree has height 4, so a search makes at most 5 comparisons, one per level, even though it holds 16 keys.

screens.title: Goal
screens.text: Trace a search in an AVL tree, and explain why it needs only O(log n) comparisons (LO3).

task.stem: In the BST lectures, how did search decide where to go next?
task.hint: This checks that you can follow a search path: compare the key with the node, then go left or right.

options.text: Visit the left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree
options.explanation: That is an in-order traversal, which visits every node. Search follows one path.

options.text: Go to the child with the smaller balance factor
options.explanation: Search never looks at balance factors. It compares keys only.

options.text: Compare the key with the node: equal, stop; smaller, go left; larger, go right
options.explanation: Right. AVL search is exactly this BST search.

screens.title: Search, step by step
screens.text: Watch the search for 30. The matching line of the pseudocode lights up at each step.
screens.caption: Compare the key with the node. Smaller: go left. Larger: go right.

screens.title: When the key is not there
screens.caption: When the next branch is empty, the key is not in the tree: return null.
steps: The right branch of 30 is empty, so 35 is not in the tree.

screens.title: Loop and recursive versions
screens.text: The loop version is the natural fit: search follows a single path from the root, so there is nothing to come back to. The recursive version does the same work: each call handles one node and calls itself on one branch only, as its last action (tail recursion).

screens.title: Why search is O(log n)
points: There is at most one comparison per level, so a search needs at most height + 1 comparisons.
Each comparison rules out one branch and everything in it. This is decrease and conquer, the same idea as binary search on a sorted array.
The AVL rule keeps the height at most roughly 1.44 log(n + 2) − 1.328.
With 1,000,000 keys, the height is at most 27, so a search needs at most 28 comparisons. A plain BST with the same keys could need 1,000,000.
screens.showRule: Comparisons ≤ height + 1, and an AVL tree’s height is O(log n).

screens.title: Search ignores balance factors
screens.caption: Search reads only the keys. The balance factors are shown here, but the pseudocode never uses them. Balance matters because it limits how long the path can be.

screens.title: Be the algorithm
screens.text: Click the next node to visit. The pseudocode line lights up and the step counter counts comparisons.

task.stem: Search for 9. Click the nodes in the order they are visited.
task.hint: This checks that you can follow a search path: compare the key with the node, then go left or right.

wrongAnswers.feedback: Check each comparison: a smaller key goes left and a larger key goes right.
Search follows one path from the root. It never visits both branches of a node.

feedback.correct: 9 > 7: go right; 9 < 13: go left; 9 < 11: go left; 9 = 9: found. That is 4 comparisons.
feedback.incorrect: 9 > 7: go right; 9 < 13: go left; 9 < 11: go left; 9 = 9: found. That is 4 comparisons.

screens.title: Be the algorithm
screens.text: The step counter never goes above 5, the height of this tree plus one.

task.stem: Search for 17. Click the nodes in the order they are visited, then choose Not found.
task.hint: This checks that you can tell when a search fails: it stops when the next branch is empty.

wrongAnswers.feedback: Check each comparison: a smaller key goes left and a larger key goes right.
Search follows one path from the root. It never visits both branches of a node.

feedback.correct: 17 > 7: go right; 17 > 13: go right; 17 > 15: go right; 17 > 16: go right. That branch is empty, so 17 is not in the tree. That is 4 comparisons.
feedback.incorrect: 17 > 7: go right; 17 > 13: go right; 17 > 15: go right; 17 > 16: go right. That branch is empty, so 17 is not in the tree. That is 4 comparisons.

screens.title: Lesson check
screens.text: One question for each assessment criterion of this lesson’s objective. Each question allows one re-attempt, and the hint is always available.

screens.title: Summary
points: AVL search is BST search: compare, then go left or right.
It stops at the key (found) or at an empty branch (not found).
At most height + 1 comparisons, and the AVL rule keeps the height O(log n).
